title: Bharata expresses his desire to proceed to Nandigrama village
introduction: After returning to Ayodhya, Bharata expresses his desire to proceed to Nandigrama village. Vasishta and the other elders agree to his proposal. Bharata along with Shatrughna ascend the chariot and proceed towards Nandigram. The ministers, family-priest, the army and the citizens of Ayodhya followed Bharata in his journey. Installing the wooden sandals of Rama on the royal throne, Bharata puts on the garb of an ascetic and carries on the rule under orders of the sandals, holding the royal canopy over them.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पंचदशोत्तरशततमः सर्गः
Thus completes 115th Chapter of Ayodhya Kanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
ततो निक्षिप्य मातृऋः स अयोध्यायाम् दृढ व्रतः |
भरतः शोक सम्तप्तो गुरून् इदम् अथ अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tato nikṣipya mātṛṛḥ sa ayodhyāyām dṛḍha vrataḥ |
bharataḥ śoka samtapto gurūn idam atha abravīt
verses.translation: Having brought his mothers back to Ayodhya; Bharata, fixed in his resolve but sore stricken with grief, spoke to Vasishta and the elders (as follows)

glosses.meaning: to Vaishta and the elders (as follows):

verses.devanagari:
नन्दि ग्रामम् गमिष्यामि सर्वान् आमन्त्रये अद्य वः |
तत्र दुह्खम् इदम् सर्वम् सहिष्ये राघवम् विना
verses.iast:
nandi grāmam gamiṣyāmi sarvān āmantraye adya vaḥ |
tatra duhkham idam sarvam sahiṣye rāghavam vinā
verses.translation: "I am going to Nandigrama village. I take leave of all of you. There, I shall be able to endure all this woe, occasioned by Rama's absence."

verses.devanagari:
गतः च हि दिवम् राजा वनस्थः च गुरुर् मम |
रामम् प्रतीक्षे राज्याय स हि राजा महा यशाः
verses.iast:
gataḥ ca hi divam rājā vanasthaḥ ca gurur mama |
rāmam pratīkṣe rājyāya sa hi rājā mahā yaśāḥ
verses.translation: "The king Dasaratha went to heaven. My elder brother is in the forest. I shall await for Rama to return to the kingdom; since verily he alone is the celebrated Lord of Ayodhya."

verses.devanagari:
एतत् श्रुत्वा शुभम् वाक्यम् भरतस्य महात्मनः |
अब्रुवन् मन्त्रिणः सर्वे वसिष्ठः च पुरोहितः
verses.iast:
etat śrutvā śubham vākyam bharatasya mahātmanaḥ |
abruvan mantriṇaḥ sarve vasiṣṭhaḥ ca purohitaḥ
verses.translation: Hearing those auspicious words of the magnanimous Bharata, Vasishta the preceptor and all the ministers spoke as follows:

verses.devanagari:
सदृशम् श्लाघनीयम् च यद् उक्तम् भरत त्वया |
वचनम् भ्रातृ वात्सल्याद् अनुरूपम् तव एव तत्
verses.iast:
sadṛśam ślāghanīyam ca yad uktam bharata tvayā |
vacanam bhrātṛ vātsalyād anurūpam tava eva tat
verses.translation: "O, Bharata! The words which your have spoken by you in devotion to your brother are very much appreciable. It is worthy of you alone."

verses.devanagari:
नित्यम् ते बन्धु लुब्धस्य तिष्ठतो भ्रातृ सौहृदे |
आर्य मार्गम् प्रपन्नस्य न अनुमन्येत कः पुमान्
verses.iast:
nityam te bandhu lubdhasya tiṣṭhato bhrātṛ sauhṛde |
ārya mārgam prapannasya na anumanyeta kaḥ pumān
verses.translation: "What man would not approve of the proposal of your highness, who are deeply fascinated of your relative, always affectionate to your brother and devoted to the path of elders?"

glosses.meaning: who are deeply fascinated of your relatives

verses.devanagari:
मन्त्रिणाम् वचनम् श्रुत्वा यथा अभिलषितम् प्रियम् |
अब्रवीत् सारथिम् वाक्यम् रथो मे युज्यताम् इति
verses.iast:
mantriṇām vacanam śrutvā yathā abhilaṣitam priyam |
abravīt sārathim vākyam ratho me yujyatām iti
verses.translation: Hearing the affectionate words of his counsellors, who spoke according to his wish, Bharata said to his charioteer, "Let my chariot be made ready!"

verses.devanagari:
प्रहृष्ट वदनः सर्वा मातृऋः समभिवाद्य सः |
आरुरोह रथम् श्रीमान् शत्रुघ्नेन समन्वितः
verses.iast:
prahṛṣṭa vadanaḥ sarvā mātṛṛḥ samabhivādya saḥ |
āruroha ratham śrīmān śatrughnena samanvitaḥ
verses.translation: The illustrious Bharata, looking pleased and having offered salutation to all his mothers, entered his chariot along with Shatrughna.

verses.devanagari:
आरुह्य तु रथम् शीघ्रम् शत्रुघ्न भरताउ उभौ |
ययतुः परम प्रीतौ वृतौ मन्त्रि पुरोहितैः
verses.iast:
āruhya tu ratham śīghram śatrughna bharatāu ubhau |
yayatuḥ parama prītau vṛtau mantri purohitaiḥ
verses.translation: Both Shatrughna and Bharata, having quickly mounted the chariot and exceedingly rejoiced, set out, accompanied by ministers and family-priests.

verses.devanagari:
अग्रतो पुरवः तत्र वसिष्ठ प्रमुखा द्विजाः |
प्रययुः प्रान् मुखाः सर्वे नन्दि ग्रामो यतो अभवत्
verses.iast:
agrato puravaḥ tatra vasiṣṭha pramukhā dvijāḥ |
prayayuḥ prān mukhāḥ sarve nandi grāmo yato abhavat
verses.translation: All the preceptors there, headed by Vasishta and other brahmanas being in the forefront, proceeded eastward, in which direction Nandigrama village was situated.

verses.devanagari:
बलम् च तद् अनाहूतम् गज अश्व रथ सम्कुलम् |
प्रययौ भरते याते सर्वे च पुर वासिनः
verses.iast:
balam ca tad anāhūtam gaja aśva ratha samkulam |
prayayau bharate yāte sarve ca pura vāsinaḥ
verses.translation: When Bharata had left, the army too, abounding in elephants, horses and chariots marched unbidden. The residents of the city also followed suit.

glosses.meaning: the residents of the city also (followed suit).

verses.devanagari:
रथस्थः स तु धर्म आत्मा भरतो भ्रातृ वत्सलः |
नन्दि ग्रामम् ययौ तूर्णम् शिरस्य् आधाय पादुके
verses.iast:
rathasthaḥ sa tu dharma ātmā bharato bhrātṛ vatsalaḥ |
nandi grāmam yayau tūrṇam śirasy ādhāya pāduke
verses.translation: The magnanimous Bharata, affectionate of his brother, bearing the sandals belong to Rama on his head, set out for Nandigrama.

verses.devanagari:
ततः तु भरतः क्षिप्रम् नन्दि ग्रामम् प्रविश्य सः |
अवतीर्य रथात् तूर्णम् गुरून् इदम् उवाच ह
verses.iast:
tataḥ tu bharataḥ kṣipram nandi grāmam praviśya saḥ |
avatīrya rathāt tūrṇam gurūn idam uvāca ha
verses.translation: Thereafter, having entered Nandigrama briskly Bharata descended his chariot quickly and spoke to his preceptors as follows:

verses.devanagari:
एतद् राज्यम् मम भ्रात्रा दत्तम् सम्न्यासवत् स्वयम् |
योग क्षेम वहे च इमे पादुके हेम भूषिते
verses.iast:
etad rājyam mama bhrātrā dattam samnyāsavat svayam |
yoga kṣema vahe ca ime pāduke hema bhūṣite
verses.translation: "My brother, Rama has given to me this kingdom as a trust. These sandals, embellished with gold diffuse gain and security to the people."

glosses.meaning: diffuse gain and security (to the people)

verses.devanagari:
भरतः शिरसा कृत्वा सन्न्यासम् पादुके ततः |
अब्रवीद्दुःखसम्तप्तः सर्वं प्रकृतिमण्डलम्
verses.iast:
bharataḥ śirasā kṛtvā sannyāsam pāduke tataḥ |
abravīdduḥkhasamtaptaḥ sarvaṃ prakṛtimaṇḍalam
verses.translation: Having dedicated the sacred trust to the wooden sandals, Bharata sore-stricken with anguish, spoke to the entire body of his ministers as follows:

verses.devanagari:
चत्रम् धारयत क्षिप्रमार्यपादाविमौ मतौ |
अभ्याम् राज्ये स्थितो धर्मः पादुकाभ्याम् गुरोर्मम
verses.iast:
catram dhārayata kṣipramāryapādāvimau matau |
abhyām rājye sthito dharmaḥ pādukābhyām gurormama
verses.translation: "Hold the state canopy speedily over these wooden sandals, which have been accepted as symbols of the feet of Rama, my noble brother. By the presence of these wooden sandals of my brother here, a piety has been established in the kingdom."

glosses.meaning: as symbols of the feet of my noble brother

verses.devanagari:
भ्रात्रा हि मयि सम्न्यासो निक्षिप्तः सौहृदादयम् |
तमिमम् पालयिष्यामि राघवागमनम् प्रति
verses.iast:
bhrātrā hi mayi samnyāso nikṣiptaḥ sauhṛdādayam |
tamimam pālayiṣyāmi rāghavāgamanam prati
verses.translation: "As a mark of compassion, this trust has been placed at my disposal, by my brother. There trust as such will be preserved till his return."

glosses.meaning: has been placed at my disposal

verses.devanagari:
क्षिप्रम् सम्योजयित्वा तु राघवस्य पुनः स्वयम् |
चरणौ तौ तु रामस्य द्रक्ष्यामि सहपादुकौ
verses.iast:
kṣipram samyojayitvā tu rāghavasya punaḥ svayam |
caraṇau tau tu rāmasya drakṣyāmi sahapādukau
verses.translation: "Having restored these wooden sandals personally to Rama's feet immediately after his return, I shall behold those feet of Rama along with these sandals."

verses.devanagari:
ततो निक्षिप्तभारोऽहम् राघवेण समागतः |
निवेद्य गुरवे राज्यम् भजिष्ये गुरुवृत्तिताम्
verses.iast:
tato nikṣiptabhāro'ham rāghaveṇa samāgataḥ |
nivedya gurave rājyam bhajiṣye guruvṛttitām
verses.translation: "Restoring the kingdom to my elder brother, when re-united with him and thereby laying down the burden, I shall then assume the role of a servant of my elder brother."

glosses.meaning: on whom thus burden has been imposed
the role of a servant of my elder brother.

verses.devanagari:
ताघवाय च सम्न्यासम् दत्त्वेमे वरपादुके |
राज्यम् चेदमयोध्याम् च धूतपापोभवामि च
verses.iast:
tāghavāya ca samnyāsam dattveme varapāduke |
rājyam cedamayodhyām ca dhūtapāpobhavāmi ca
verses.translation: "By giving away these excellent wooden sandals, the symbols of trust, this kingdom, as well as the City of Ayodhya to Rama, I shall be washed of all my sins."

glosses.meaning: as well as the city of Ayodhya

verses.devanagari:
अभिषिक्ते तु काकुत्थ्से प्रहृष्टमुदिते जने |
प्रीतिर्मम यशश्चैव भवेद्राज्याच्चतुर्गुणम्
verses.iast:
abhiṣikte tu kākutthse prahṛṣṭamudite jane |
prītirmama yaśaścaiva bhavedrājyāccaturguṇam
verses.translation: "Rama will be installed and his subjects made happy. It will be a four-fold more fame and happiness for me than that having obtained from the kingdom."

glosses.meaning: than (that having obtained) from the kingdom.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् तु विलपन्धीनो भरतः स महायशाः |
नन्दिग्रामेऽकरोद्राज्यम् दुःखितो मन्त्रिभिस्सह
verses.iast:
evam tu vilapandhīno bharataḥ sa mahāyaśāḥ |
nandigrāme'karodrājyam duḥkhito mantribhissaha
verses.translation: The highly illustrious Bharata though a distressed man, thus lamenting and pained, looked after the state administration along with his ministers from Nandigrama.

verses.devanagari:
स वल्कलजटाधारी मुनिवेषधरः प्रभुः |
नन्दिग्रामेऽवसद्वीरः ससैन्यो भरतस्तदा
verses.iast:
sa valkalajaṭādhārī muniveṣadharaḥ prabhuḥ |
nandigrāme'vasadvīraḥ sasainyo bharatastadā
verses.translation: Assuming bark robes and matted locks in the guise of an ascetic, the lord and the hero Bharata dwelt in Nandigrama, protected by the army.

glosses.meaning: Assuming bark robes and matted locks
in the guise of an ascetic

verses.devanagari:
रामागमनमाकाङ्क्षन् भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः |
भ्रातुर्वचनकारी च प्रतिज्ञापारगस्तदा
पादुके त्वभिषिच्याथ नन्दिग्रामेऽवसत्तथा |
verses.iast:
rāmāgamanamākāṇ^kṣan bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ |
bhrāturvacanakārī ca pratijJṇāpāragastadā
pāduke tvabhiṣicyātha nandigrāme'vasattathā |
verses.translation: Bharata, obedient to his elder brother, affectionate of his brothers and faithful to his vow, thus resided in Nandigrama, coronating the wooden sandals on the throne and wishing always for the return of Rama.

glosses.meaning: the wooden sandals ( on the throne)

verses.devanagari:
स वालव्यजनम् चत्रम् धारयामास स स्वयम्
भरतः शासनम् सर्वम् पादुकाभ्याम् निवेदयन् |
verses.iast:
sa vālavyajanam catram dhārayāmāsa sa svayam
bharataḥ śāsanam sarvam pādukābhyām nivedayan |
verses.translation: Reporting all the royal orders to the wooden sandals, Bharata was holding the royal canopy together with the chowrie to those sandals.

glosses.meaning: together with the chowrie (to the sandals)

verses.devanagari:
ततस्तु भरतः श्रीमानभिषिच्यार्यपादुके
तदधीनस्तदा राज्यम् कारयामास सर्वदा |
verses.iast:
tatastu bharataḥ śrīmānabhiṣicyāryapāduke
tadadhīnastadā rājyam kārayāmāsa sarvadā |
verses.translation: Coronating the wooden sandals of his elder brother, the illustrious Bharata thereafter carried out the state administration, always maintaining his subservience to them.

glosses.meaning: the wooden sandals of his elder brother

verses.devanagari:
तदा हि यत्कार्यमुपैति किंचि |
दुपायनम् चोपहृतम् महार्हम् |
स पादुकाभ्याम् प्रथमम् निवेद्य |
चकार पश्चाद्भरतो यथावत्
verses.iast:
tadā hi yatkāryamupaiti kiṃci |
dupāyanam copahṛtam mahārham |
sa pādukābhyām prathamam nivedya |
cakāra paścādbharato yathāvat
verses.translation: Whatever a small affair of the state came up or whenever a high-valued gift was offered, Bharata used to report that matter to the wooden sandals and then only dealt with it in the proper way afterwards.
